explanations.explanation: The crowds are amazed, just like the verse says. A man who couldn't speak is suddenly talking, and I'd have dropped a whole tray of cookies on the spot. Hold on to that amazement, friend. The next verse shows it didn't land the same way for everybody.

Running away isn't what the verse says. The crowds are amazed when the man who had been mute spoke (Luke 11:14). I think a man talking after being mute would make anybody drop what they're doing. Save the running for when the oven timer goes off.

Telling Him to leave isn't what the verse says. The crowds are amazed when the man who had been mute spoke. Some of them do say something against Him in the very next verse, but that's a different thing. Here, the verse gives us amazement.

Right, they call Beelzebul the prince of the demons. So some people watched a man get his voice back and said the power behind it was the ruler of demons. Friend, that is a WILD thing to say. Jesus is about to answer them.

The king of Tyre never shows up in this scene. The people who say it call Beelzebul the prince of the demons. Mix-ups happen, and I once stamped a whole batch upside down. Keep the title in mind, because Jesus answers it directly.

No captain of the guard here. The accusers say Beelzebul is the prince of the demons, the one in charge of them. That's the claim they make about where Jesus gets His power. It's a big claim, and Jesus has a big answer for it.
A sign it is. Others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven. A man had just started talking, and they asked for something on top of that. The text calls it testing, friend.
A voice isn't what they ask for. The text says they demand a sign from heaven. A man who could not speak a moment ago has just spoken, and they're asking for something on top of that.
No fire is requested here. The others test Jesus by demanding a sign from heaven. Fire would be a pretty dramatic order, but the text keeps it to a sign. I only ask for fire from my ovens.

That's what Jesus says: every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste. He adds that a house divided against a house will fall. Picture two people yanking one cookie sheet in opposite directions. Nobody gets cookies, friend, just a floor full of crumbs.
Jesus says the opposite. A kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall. Splitting up doesn't add strength in this picture. It takes it away.

No treaty in this picture, friend. Jesus says every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall. I've heard of a lot of ways to settle things, but the verse doesn't hand this kingdom a pen and paper.

Their judges, exactly. Jesus says, "And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges." He asks about their own sons, and then names those sons as the judges. I'd say that's a smooth move.
Jesus doesn't call them servants. He asks by whom their sons drive out demons, and says they will be the accusers' judges. Their own sons end up weighing in on the accusation. That's quite a turn.
Teachers isn't the word Jesus uses. He asks by whom their sons drive out demons, and then says, "So then, they will be your judges." Judges, friend, not teachers.

Kingdom, yes. Jesus says if He drives out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon them. He's answering the accusation head on. That's a lot to say about one man who just started talking.

Wrath isn't the word, friend. Jesus says, "But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you." I'll admit wrath sounds dramatic, like burning the whole batch on purpose. But the verse says kingdom.
Not the day, friend. Jesus says, "But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you." It's an if-then, and the then is kingdom, not day.

explanations.answer: He overpowers him and takes away his armor
explanations.explanation: That's how Jesus tells it. Someone stronger attacks and overpowers the strong man, and takes away the armor he trusted. Then he divides up the plunder. The fully armed man had everything lined up, and it still wasn't enough against someone stronger.

explanations.answer: He is driven off by the strong man's armor
explanations.explanation: The armor doesn't win in this picture. The stronger man overpowers the strong man and takes away that very armor. The strong man trusted it, and it didn't hold. Armor is only as good as the one wearing it.

explanations.answer: He makes peace and leaves the house alone
explanations.explanation: No peace talks in this picture. Jesus says the stronger man attacks, overpowers the strong man, takes his armor and divides up his plunder. Nobody leaves the house alone. It's a one-sided ending.
True. Jesus says, “He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.” There's no standing in the middle here. Either you're gathering with Him or you're scattering.

This one is actually true. Jesus says, “He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.” Both halves are in the verse. It's a short line, and an easy one to read past.
House is right. The spirit passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, "I will return to the house I left." So it heads back to the place it came from.
City isn't the word. The spirit says it will return to the house it left. Jesus keeps the picture going with a house all the way through. Houses are a theme in this passage.
No tomb here. The spirit says, "I will return to the house I left." It's a house, and it will matter in a moment what shape that house is in.

explanations.answer: Brings seven spirits more wicked than itself
explanations.explanation: Seven spirits more wicked than itself, that's what Jesus says. They go in and dwell there. The house was swept clean and put in order, and still it gets new tenants, and these are more wicked than the first. Jesus says, "And the final plight of that man is worse than the first."

explanations.answer: Brings two spirits weaker than itself
explanations.explanation: The number is seven, and they aren't weaker. Jesus says the spirit brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself. They all go in and dwell there. It goes the opposite way from what you picked.

explanations.answer: Leaves the house and never comes back
explanations.explanation: It does come back. In fact, it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself. Then they go in and dwell there. The house doesn't get left alone.
It's the other way around. Jesus says the final plight of that man is worse than the first. He ends up worse off than where he started. That's the end of the picture.
False, you've got it. Jesus says, "And the final plight of that man is worse than the first." It's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly. The man doesn't end up better off.

explanations.answer: Those who hear the word of God and obey it
explanations.explanation: Yes. Jesus replies, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” A woman in the crowd lifted her voice with a blessing, and He pointed to hearing and obeying. That's the one to take home with you.

explanations.answer: Those who pray and fast in the temple daily
explanations.explanation: Praying and fasting in the temple isn't what Jesus names. He replies, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” A woman in the crowd had just blessed the womb that bore Him, and He pointed to hearing and obeying. Even I, surrounded by cookies all day, can't fast my way into that answer.

explanations.answer: Those who give to the poor and tell no one
explanations.explanation: Giving to the poor and telling no one is a nice thought, but it isn't what Jesus names. He replies, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” A woman in the crowd had just blessed the womb that bore Him, and He turned to those who hear and obey. Even my best secret cookie delivery doesn't make that list.

True. Jesus says, “For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So He's talking about Himself when He says the Son of Man will be a sign.
That's actually true. Jesus says, "For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation." Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

Greater, yes. Jesus says, “…now One greater than Solomon is here.” The Queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Jesus is saying someone even greater is here now.
Younger isn't the word, friend. Jesus says One greater than Solomon is here. The queen came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, so the comparison is about greatness, not age.
Poorer isn't it. The Queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and Jesus says One greater than Solomon is here. Money isn't part of the comparison, friend.

It goes the other way. Jesus says the Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them. She came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom. She's not there to defend them.

False, correct. Jesus says the Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them. She came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Now One greater than Solomon is here.

explanations.answer: They repented at the preaching of Jonah
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Jesus gives. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here. Nineveh listened to Jonah's preaching, and Jesus says someone greater is here now.

explanations.answer: They tore down the idols in their city
explanations.explanation: Idols aren't mentioned here. Jesus says the men of Nineveh will condemn this generation because they repented at the preaching of Jonah. That's the reason He names. Stick with what He says.

explanations.answer: They built an altar to the God of Israel
explanations.explanation: No altar in this verse, friend. Building one is a big project, and Jesus doesn't list it. He says the men of Nineveh will condemn this generation because they repented at the preaching of Jonah.

explanations.answer: So those who enter can see the light
explanations.explanation: That's the reason Jesus gives. A lamp goes on a stand so those who enter can see the light. A lamp has a job, and hiding it in a cellar defeats the whole point. It's like baking a fresh batch and hiding the tray in a closet while the guests wait.

explanations.answer: So the flame stays safe from the wind
explanations.explanation: Wind isn't the reason Jesus gives. He says the lamp goes on a stand so those who enter can see the light. The stand is about people seeing, not the flame being protected.

explanations.answer: So the oil lasts through the night
explanations.explanation: Oil isn't part of the picture, friend. Jesus says no one puts a lit lamp in a cellar or under a basket, but sets it on a stand so those who enter can see the light. The reason is the seeing, not how long the lamp burns. Nobody's checking the oil gauge in this verse.

True. Jesus says, "When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light." He goes on to say that when they are bad, the body is full of darkness. So the eye is like the lamp for the whole body.
This one is true. Jesus says, "When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light." He calls the eye the lamp of your body. Good eyes, full of light.

Darkness, yes. Jesus says, "Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness." It's a warning to check on the light. I sat for years in the back of a dark junk drawer, so I'll tell you I'd rather have the light on.
Borrowed isn't the word. Jesus says, "Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness." The warning is that the light within might be darkness. Borrowing doesn't come into it.
Wasted isn't what Jesus says. He says, "Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness." The warning is that the light within might be darkness. Wasted isn't in the verse, friend.

explanations.answer: Radiant as though a lamp were shining on you
explanations.explanation: Radiant, just like Jesus says. If your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you. It's a picture of being lit up from head to toe. No dark corners anywhere.

explanations.answer: Wise as though you had heard Solomon speak
explanations.explanation: Solomon came up earlier, but not in this line. Jesus says you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you. This verse is about light, not wisdom. The lamp picture finishes right here.

explanations.answer: Warm as though you sat beside a fire
explanations.explanation: A fire isn't in this verse. Jesus says you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you. The picture stays with the lamp from start to finish. Radiant is the word.
